Despite strong demand, the supply of used EVs remains limited, representing only 1.6% of 3-year-old vehicle inventory in Q3, a factor that contributes to their quick turnover. <5> Market analyses from Q4 2025 indicate a strengthening buyer's market for used vehicles, supported by several key trends observed in October. According to Cox Automotive's Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index, seasonally adjusted wholesale used-vehicle prices fell by 2.0% in October compared to September. Non-adjusted prices saw an even steeper decline of 3.7% from the previous month. Concurrently, used vehicle inventory has been on the rise. At the beginning of October, the total supply of used vehicles on dealer lots was 2.26 million units, a 10% increase from the previous year. This led to a wholesale supply of 28 days and a retail days' supply of 48, the first time in 2025 that the supply has been higher than the previous year. A slowdown in retail sales contributed to this inventory growth, with sales declining over 5% from August to September. While some analysts note that tighter supply and solid demand toward the end of October could lead to lower depreciation for the rest of Q4, the overall conditions of falling wholesale prices and rising inventory point towards a market favorable to buyers heading into the end of the year. <6> In October, the Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index (MUVVI) saw its most significant depreciation of 2025, falling 2.0% from September to a value of 202.9. This decline reflects a drop in wholesale used-vehicle prices, adjusted for mix, mileage, and seasonality. Despite the sharp monthly decrease, the index was nearly unchanged compared to October 2024. Unadjusted for seasonal factors, wholesale prices were down 3.7% from the previous month but remained 0.2% higher than the previous year. According to Cox Automotive's Deputy Chief Economist, this level of depreciation is typical for October as dealers reduce activity before winter and a higher mix of new model-year vehicles enters the retail inventory. Several vehicle categories saw declines, with electric vehicle (EV) values dropping 3.0% for the month, though they remained up 3.9% year-over-year. <7> Citing data from vAuto Live Market View, retail used-vehicle sales in September 2025 experienced a 5.2% decrease from August, with dealers selling an estimated 1.42 million units. This slowdown is attributed to affordability challenges and seasonal trends. Despite the monthly drop from 1.50 million sales in August, the market showed a 6.6% increase compared to September of the previous year. Concurrently, used-vehicle inventory levels reached a new high for 2025, rising to 2.26 million vehicles at the beginning of October. This increase in inventory led to a higher days' supply of 48, up from previous months. <8> Ford has issued a safety recall for a total of nine 2025 model year Bronco and Ranger vehicles due to improperly bonded windshields. According to the recall notice, the windshields may not have been correctly secured, posing a safety risk as they could detach during a crash and increase the likelihood of injury. Ford planned to begin mailing owner notification letters on October 20, 2025, with one source indicating notifications could extend to October 24. <9> Toyota has announced a major safety recall affecting approximately 394,000 vehicles in the U.S., specifically covering 2022-2025 Tundra and Tundra Hybrid models, as well as 2023-2025 Sequoia Hybrids. The recall addresses a software bug in the 14-inch center display that can cause the rearview camera image to fail when the vehicle is placed in reverse. Affected drivers may see a half-green, full-green, or completely black screen, which significantly reduces rearward visibility and increases the risk of a collision. Dealerships will fix the issue by installing a free software update. Toyota expects to mail notification letters to affected vehicle owners by November 30, 2025.
